action: State and local IT leaders: confirm whether your organisation still has MS-ISAC coverage, directly or through a statewide membership, and plan alternative threat feeds if not.
exec: Thousands of US local governments and school districts no longer receive shared threat intelligence and monitoring they previously had for free.
plain: The group that shares cyber threat warnings with US cities, counties and schools has lost about two-thirds of its members since it began charging fees.
summary: The threat-sharing body for US state and local governments has nearly 6,000 members, including 20 state governments, down from a peak above 18,000 before federal funding ended and membership became paid. An interim board is reviewing its mission and core services: threat intelligence, peer collaboration and a round-the-clock security operations centre.
title: MS-ISAC down to about a third of its membership a year into paid model

validation.note: One outlet interviewing an MS-ISAC executive.

review.note: Nearly 6,000 members incl. 20 states, peak above 18,000, interim board and three core services match GovTech (12 Nov). Published 12 Nov, just outside the 6-day window.
